class_id: a third-party API/page's empty-result response was assumed, never observed, and a test fake baked the wrong assumption in
feature: any scraper or integration reading a third-party search/list endpoint whose zero-result shape was never captured live (SEBI DRHP search: www.sebi.gov.in listing search)
symptom: a caller assumes a third party signals "nothing found" the way a REST API would (404, an empty array, a distinct error code). Many web-era government/exchange sites instead answer every query, hit or miss, with HTTP 200 and the same listing page shell; the only distinguishing marker is inside the HTML (a table present vs. a `No record(s) available.` sentence). When the code -- or worse, a test's hand-written fake server -- assumes the wrong shape (e.g. a fake that always returns a table, or code that treats 200 as "found"), a real empty result reads as success with 0 usable rows, or a dead/expired session reads as a legitimate empty result, and neither is distinguishable from the other without reading the marker.
first_seen:
2026-09-27/29 -- IPODhan, SEBI DRHP search page (www.sebi.gov.in). Live capture 2026-09-29: a nonexistent-filer query ("zzqx nonexistent") returns HTTP 200 with the listing page's own form[name="homeForm"], no table#sample_1, and the marker `

No record(s) available.

` inside `.pagination_inner`; a real filer ("deepa jewellers") returns HTTP 200 with table#sample_1 holding 1 row. A fake test server used earlier in this area always returned a table, which hid the zero-result shape from every test that exercised it (F-198, docs/design/findings.json). Fixed alongside the #620 discovery-budget fix, PR #1276, with a live-captured fixture (scraper/tests/fixtures/sebi/sebi-drhp-search-no-records.html) replacing the fake.
fix_prs: #1276 (fix/620-document-budget-drain) -- adds the live-captured no-records fixture and a test asserting the marker is read, not assumed
detection_check: the #1276 fixture test asserts SEBI's specific zero-result marker on this one endpoint. No general check exists for the wider shape: a repo-wide sweep for third-party integrations whose zero-result fixture is a live capture (not hand-typed) versus ones still relying on an assumption or a synthetic fake
status: guarded for the SEBI DRHP search page only (#1276's live fixture); every OTHER third-party endpoint's empty-result shape in the scraper is unguarded against the same wrong-assumption failure -- generalising to a repo-wide live-fixture requirement is the obvious extension, not taken here
